data.head: ## The installed CLI bundles, read as strings (a READING, not a measurement)

body:
Read from `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.328/claude` and `…/2.1.330/claude` with `strings -n 8`, the
window around each name read whole. Minified names differ per version; the shapes below are the same in both.

- **The hard per-call limit.** `di(e)` (2.1.330) / `ii(e)` (2.1.328): the server config's `timeout` when it is a
  number ≥ 1000, else the env `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, else `1e8` ms (`var km=1e8` / `var Lm=1e8`, 7 368 bytes before
  the function in both bundles), clamped to at least 1000 and at most a module constant (a standalone
  `var au=2147483647;` / `var eu=2147483647;` string stands in each bundle; the binding to the clamp is read by
  name only, unproven). The schema text the CLI ships beside it: «Per-server tool-call timeout in milliseconds.
  Overrides the MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT environment variable for this server. Hard wall-clock limit per call; progress
  notifications do not extend it. Values below 1000ms are ignored (falls through to MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the
  default).» The default `1e8` ms is about 27.8 hours.

- **The idle limit.** `Kl(e)` (both): for a `stdio` server `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` else `1800000` ms
  (30 min); `300000` ms for other remote types; `0` for `sse-ide` / `ws-ide` / `sdk` (an `sdk` server has its own
  arm); `≤ 0` disables; then clamped to at least the per-server `timeout` and at most the hard limit. A 30 s
  watchdog tick aborts the call when no response or progress notification came for that long; a progress
  notification resets the idle clock (`St=Date.now()` in `onprogress`), never the hard limit.

- **At the bound.** The hard limit rejects the one call with an error of class «MCP tool timeout», message
  `MCP server "{server}" tool "{tool}" timed out after {n}s` plus a fixed sentence that the outcome is unknown and
  must be checked before a repeat; the idle abort is «MCP tool idle timeout» with its own message; both carry
  `mcpErrorSource: "downstream_unreachable"`. Nothing read shows the server torn down at either bound — the call
  alone is rejected; a teardown is UNREAD, not read absent.

- **Auto-background.** Both bundles hold `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS`: unset, a gate (`tengu_mcp_auto_background`,
  default true) gives `120000` ms; `sse-ide` / `ws-ide` and an `sdk` server with `disableAutoBackground` are excluded,
  a stdio server is not; a non-interactive session runs it only under `CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS`. Its effect on a
  call past 120 s (the call moved to a background task, the turn going on) is read from the gate's shape only.

- **The 60 s floor.** `ou(e)` (2.1.330) / `Zl(e)` (2.1.328) floors at `60000` ms the per-request timeout of the
  HTTP transports — the only 60 s figure read; it is not the stdio call's limit on these two versions.

- **The names that move it** (names only): the per-server `timeout` key of an MCP server's config; env
  `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS`,
  `CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND`; the gate `tengu_mcp_auto_background`.

- **What only a start tells:** that the client applies this bound to a real call of a stdio server as read —
  the error class it returns, the elapsed seconds, whether the server is torn down, and whether a call past 120 s
  in an interactive driver is backgrounded rather than failed.

body:
- **send** — client side: the text checks, the strict-modes and liveness reads, a socket connect, a
  `spawn_blocking` start-time read: unbounded in code, bounded in practice by local file and socket calls. Wrapper
  side: the readiness gate ≤ `GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s, the flight guard (held by the hook tap's short sections and
  by another send's paste), the paste (no deadline: a 16 MiB text into a child not reading its PTY blocks
  without end), then the window, 10 s or 40 s for `/compact`. The compiled sum is 8.5 + 40 = 48.5 s plus the
  paste; the MCP side waits on the reply with no deadline, so a stalled wrapper holds the call until the
  client's own bound.

- **wait** — `timeout_ms` = min(given, 50 000) (`wait_timeout`, tools.rs:46), run by the wrapper's own clock;
  the MCP side again adds no deadline.
- **last** — one reply read from disk by the wrapper; no wait.

   maps to it (`src/cmd/client.rs` maps its own enum into the set and gains no arm).

2. **The client-bound reading.** `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` (the only crate that knows Claude) gains
   `MCP_CLIENT_BOUND_READ: Duration` = 120 s, its doc comment saying it is a READING of the 2.1.328 and 2.1.330
   bundles' strings — the auto-background default, the tightest client bound read; the stdio hard limit 1e8 ms and
   the stdio idle limit 1 800 000 ms named beside it as read — never a measurement.

3. **The deadline.** `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`: `pub const MCP_CALL_DEADLINE: Duration` = 55 s. `frame()`'s
   whole body (the instance check, the liveness read, the socket-directory check, the connect, the peer checks, the
   request and its reply) runs under the deadline: whichever ends first, the frame's result or the deadline, decides;
   at the deadline the result is `result::unreachable(UnreachableCause::CallDeadline)` and the frame's future is
   dropped (its connection closes; the wrapper's own work is not cancelled). The deadline comes from an injected seam
   held by the server: a function giving a future that ends at the deadline — in production Tokio's `sleep` of
   `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`; in a test a signal the test fires (tests S3: time only through an injected seam, no paused
   Tokio clock). `crates/viola-mcp/src/lib.rs`: `Tools::new` keeps its signature and uses the production seam;
   `Tools::with_deadline(home, own_name, list, deadline)` takes the seam (the handlers suite's door); re-export
   `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`. `list` is not a frame tool and keeps its 5 s-bounded agents read, unchanged.

4. **Tokio's timer.** `crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml`: tokio `features = ["rt", "time"]`. `Cargo.lock` gains no
   package (the feature adds no crate; read `git diff --stat Cargo.lock` after the build: no line). The sole-root
   bans and `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` stay green (entries 8, 9).

    the round. A red start is analysed from its ledger line before anything else runs; the spare is spent only on a
    start refused or lost to a cause outside the reading (a host contention, a rig refusal, an account limit) —
    never on a red reading. A fourth base start is the operator's. On an account-limit refusal implement stops where
    it is (`inputs#I2` item 11).

14. After the span: the census keyed `operator`; the ledger's three summaries copied into
    `evidence/live-round.md` (entry 28, report-only), the `outlived` reading among them; entry 27 is the census.
15. The whole integration layer, the smoke, `pre-push`, hygiene, the push and CI (entries 29–36).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mcpcall.rs` — the stream-json reader into closed words, with its inline cases
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` — `UnreachableCause::CallDeadline` / `call-deadline` and its case row
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `MCP_CLIENT_BOUND_READ`, the reading's constant
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` — `MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`, the deadline over `frame()`, the injected seam, `WAIT_CAP`'s comment, the bound's unit case
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/lib.rs` — `Tools::with_deadline`, the re-export
- `crates/viola-mcp/src/result.rs` — the cause table case gains `CallDeadline`
- `crates/viola-mcp/Cargo.toml` — tokio's `time` feature
- `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs` — the held reply, the two deadline cases
- `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — the new writer named, if the census asks
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `Arm::MB`, its labels, `Plan.fake`, the arm, the table cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — `--fake`, the labels in the doc
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the `MB` rehearsals

The block runs: phase A (formatter, linter, the three crates' units, the viola-mcp suite, the call-deadline control's
filtered entry, the error-bodies census, the tokio and rmcp gates); phase B (the rig library cases, the `MB`
rehearsals through the integration layer, which builds the root binaries they spawn); the round (entries 14–26,
`round` and `live` entries ONLY, `inputs#I2` item 10), its after-reads of state other actors move keyed to the
round; after the span the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole layers and the
operator pass. What is not run, and why: no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's
`release` job runs it); `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job (no dependency is added, a feature only; the
tokio bans are entries 8–9). Every test start runs under a test-owned home; every waiting test takes a bound under
the 20 s lint, the handlers' held reply a 5 s backstop. The live starts run under the rig's private scratch and
config; the rig's `--deadline` bounds each under its entry's `timeout`. The non-priming probes of each live leg are
the round entries ahead of it. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card.
**The remove-the-guard control** is implement's one-shot `gate.py control`, never an entry:
| | `call-deadline` |
| **File** | `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` |
| **The edit removes** | the deadline over `frame()`: the frame awaited alone, the seam's future never polled |
| **Case** | `handlers_frame_tools_end_at_the_call_deadline::case_1_send` |
| **Fired on** | entry 6, `--timeout 300` |

With the guard removed the call returns the canned reply at the wrapper's 5 s backstop, the case reads its detail
red, and no `TIMEOUT` line can stand for it (300 s against a 5 s backstop); a `timeout` reading would NOT read the
guard as held. The filter selects 0 tests on the untouched tree and the four cases once they exist.
